title: Write and Run Your First Playbook
objective: Translate an ad-hoc package operation into a named, repeatable YAML play.

sourceAlignment.title: Getting started with Ansible 06 - Writing our first Playbook
sourceAlignment.creator: LearnLinuxTV
sourceAlignment.note: English captions informed topic alignment and timestamps. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A playbook binds a host pattern to ordered tasks. Each task has a descriptive name and invokes a module that declares the required state.
YAML indentation expresses structure, so align play-level keys and nest module arguments consistently. Use fully qualified module names even when short names work; they make intent unambiguous.

The play recap separates ok, changed, unreachable, failed, rescued, ignored, and skipped outcomes. Run the play twice: the second recap is the simplest first check that your automation converges cleanly.
explanation.rule: A healthy state-setting playbook succeeds twice and reports changed=0 on the second run.

examples.title: Working design or automation artifact
examples.code:
- name: Configure web servers
  hosts: webservers
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Install nginx
      ansible.builtin.package:
        name: nginx
        state: present
examples.note: Read the structure, predict its effect, then adapt it in the assignment and terminal mission.

checks.question: Which practice best supports this lesson’s objective: “Translate an ad-hoc package operation into a named, repeatable YAML play.”?
options: Preview scope, use state-aware modules, and verify the observed result.
Hide failures and assume the target state was reached.
Store credentials beside the playbook in plaintext.
Replace every module with an unreviewed shell command.

feedback.correct: Correct—safe automation combines explicit scope, desired state, and verification.
feedback.incorrect: The reliable workflow makes scope, state, and verification visible.

assignment.title: Build the Web Playbook
assignment.brief: Install nginx on webservers with an elevated, named task.
requirements: Include every named safety or behavior requirement.
assignment.starterCode:
- name: Configure web servers
  hosts: webservers
assignment.solutionCode:
- name: Configure web servers
  hosts: webservers
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Install nginx
      ansible.builtin.package:
        name: nginx
        state: present
    - name: Start nginx
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: nginx
        state: started
assignment.outputCheckLabel: Artifact uses valid course-style YAML structure

steps: Run it twice and compare the recaps.
